summary.oneLiner: A standout quarter, new factoring/TReDS and adjacent optionality (insurance broking, LAP, GIFT City, AIF/ARC), all built with conservative, zero-NPA discipline.

one-line thesis: A standout quarter — **record quarterly PBT of Rs 72 cr (+27% QoQ)** on a loan book that hit **Rs 4,552 cr (+82% YoY, +16% QoQ)** while holding **nil NPAs**, 32% CAR and a lean 7% cost-to-income. The APL-Apollo-seeded supply-chain NBFC is deliberately under-committing: it guides to **~Rs 300 cr FY27 PBT (~75% YoY)** with **no equity raise needed to Rs 10,000 cr AUM**, and is levering up (2.0x→3.0x over ~2 yrs) to push ROE from 14% toward 16%. The story is diversification off the parent (APL Apollo now only ~1/3 of AUM), new factoring/TReDS and adjacent optionality (insurance broking, LAP, GIFT City, AIF/ARC) — all built with conservative, zero-NPA discipline.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY / QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| PBT | Rs 72 cr | **+27% QoQ** (highest ever) | annualized run-rate ~Rs 280–290 cr with no growth |
| PAT (implied) | ~Rs 54 cr | — | ~Rs 300 cr PBT → ~Rs 225 cr PAT for FY27 |
| Loan book / AUM | Rs 4,552 cr | **+82% YoY, +16% QoQ** | ~Rs 4,000 cr average book in Q1; disbursed >Rs 7,000 cr (high-churn) |
| Net worth | Rs 1,539 cr (30-Jun) | — | boosted by ~Rs 337 cr warrant equity received Mar–Apr (+Rs 20 cr warrant conversion in Apr) |
| Leverage | 2.2x | vs 1.9x on 31-Mar | targeting transit to 3.0x |
| CAR | 32% | — | ample headroom |
| ROA (annualized) | 5.1% | stabilized ~5% | 1% opex, low credit cost |
| ROE (annualized) | 14% | vs 12% FY26 | target 16% at 3x leverage |
| Asset quality | **nil NPA** | maintained | supply-chain = inherently low credit cost |
| Cost-to-income | 7% | opex ~1% of avg book | guidance: keep <15% |
| Avg portfolio yield | 12.5% | stable (Q3/Q4/Q1) | factoring neither dilutive nor accretive |
| Per-employee profit | >Rs 2 cr/yr | — | lean, digital-first structure |
> Factoring outstanding Rs 225 cr in Jun (vs Rs 175 cr Mar), ~5% of AUM. 52 anchor mandates; Rs 7,700 cr of signed MoUs (mgmt flags MoU as a "dummy limit" — no book visibility). +5 new anchor mandates in Q1.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **FY27 PBT ~Rs 300 cr** (≈75% YoY growth) → **~Rs 225 cr PAT**; FY27-exit **equity ~Rs 1,700 cr**, **AUM ~Rs 5,500 cr** (Rs 6,000 cr "aspirational").
- **AUM CAGR 25–30%** and **profitability CAGR 30–35%** over the next 3–4 years.
- **FY30 AUM target Rs 10,000 cr** (raised from earlier Rs 7,500 cr / Rs 375 cr PAT FY30 guidance; may be hit in FY29). Excludes FY26 base.
- **No equity raise** up to Rs 10,000 cr AUM — funded organically via retained profit + leverage.
- **Leverage 2.0x → 3.0x over ~2 years**, driving **ROE 14% → 16%**; **ROA maintained 4.5–5%**; **cost-to-income kept <15%**.
- Forward QoQ pace: **PAT ~8–10% QoQ**, **AUM ~15–16% QoQ** (the 27% QoQ PBT jump is not repeatable — distorted by ~Rs 337 cr equity that landed end-Mar/early-Apr, absent in Q4).
- **SG Insurance Brokers** (fee-based, B2B cross-sell): IRDAI application pending → launch **not before Q4 FY27** ("2–3 quarters away").
order book & pipeline: No traditional order book (revolving credit). Pipeline = 52 anchor mandates (Rs 7,700 cr MoUs, treated as soft), deepening (more dealers per anchor + new products like factoring on existing channel-finance anchors) and widening (new anchors/geographies/products). TAM framed as ~Rs 25 lakh cr of receivables on the top-1,000 corporates' balance sheets (their estimate of the addressable sales-side financing market).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Business mix:** ~2/3 working-capital / supply-chain / factoring (bouquet across MSMEs + corporates); ~1/3 beyond supply chain (LAP cross-sell + opportunistic). **No retail/consumer financing.**
- **APL Apollo ecosystem** ~1/3 of AUM (lower in Jun quarter); mgmt frames the book as ~1/3 APL-Apollo supply chain, ~1/3 non-APL working capital, ~1/3 beyond supply chain. Dependency on parent falling as SGFIN outgrows APL Apollo.
- **Factoring (Rs 225 cr, ~5% AUM):** two legs — TReDS (very competitive, yields at par with channel finance) and bilateral factoring (par to slightly higher). RBI factoring licence held; senior team hired in Mumbai/Delhi/Kolkata. Grows in industries where channel finance is nascent (unlike matured auto/steel).
- **SG Insurance Brokers** (WoS): fee-only broker (not underwriter), B2B cross-sell to ecosystem borrowers/anchors (keyman, group health, trade-credit); IRDAI pending; ≥2–3 quarters out.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Digital lending** and **LAP** (leveraging the MSME + digital stack and 30-location team) — clearly on the roadmap.
- **GIFT City** international supply-chain finance — long-term, subject to dual RBI + IFSCA approval; tax advantages.
- **AIF (wealth management) and ARC** — board approvals obtained; part of a 5–10-yr vision to be a "comprehensive financial solution provider" spanning supply chain, lending, equity/broking.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Cost + credit-quality moat:** supply-chain finance is a high-churn, low-credit-cost niche served by "less than 1% of banks and NBFCs"; SGFIN's zero-NPA record across ~4 years (Oct-2022 inception to ~Rs 4,552 cr book) plus ~1% opex and 12.5% stable yield is the evidenced edge. Fills the residual working-capital gap banks/large NBFCs won't underwrite (appetite/policy caps), so it competes on availability of the marginal rupee rather than price.
- **Parent-ecosystem origination:** APL Apollo genesis gave a captive anchor base to "find its feet," now diversified to ~1/3 dependency — a warm-start distribution advantage.
margins & cost dynamics: ROA stabilized at ~5% (5.1% in Q1); ~1% opex-to-average-book maintained (Q4 and Q1 both ~1%); cost-to-income optically low at 7% but mgmt guides to the more meaningful <15% ceiling. Yield stable at 12.5% — factoring has been neither dilutive nor accretive. Lean team + digital leverage → per-employee profit >Rs 2 cr.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Asset-light NBFC — "expansion" = licences/entities (insurance broker incorporated; AIF/ARC/GIFT-City board-approved) and geographic/product widening. Watch slippage on: SG Insurance Brokers launch (guided ≥Q4 FY27), GIFT City (dual-regulator approval, long-dated), and the AUM ramp to Rs 5,500 cr FY27-exit.
capital allocation:
- **No equity dilution** planned to Rs 10,000 cr AUM — growth self-funded from retained earnings + a deliberate lever-up (2.0x→3.0x). ~Rs 337 cr warrant equity received Mar–Apr already in the base.
- ESOP: 20-lakh-option pool (shareholder-approved); ~10.32 lakh granted Apr-2026, ~50k new-joiner grants now, ~9 lakh unallotted; direct company allotment (no trust). New pools only with fresh shareholder approval.
risks & watch-items:
- **Geopolitical/war uncertainty** compressing MSME/SME incremental working-capital demand — a *business* (growth) risk, not yet a credit risk; forces reliance on new-customer/product acquisition.
- **Lending-business tail risk:** nil NPA is an aspiration, not a guarantee — mgmt explicitly concedes losses "may happen in future"; conservative net-worth build is the shock absorber.
- **Guidance conservatism gap:** growing 82% YoY but guiding 25–30% — repeated analyst pushback; execution/over-delivery vs sandbagging to watch.
- Concentration to APL Apollo (~1/3) and reliance on a still-small (Rs 4,552 cr) base.
management quality / tone: Confident but deliberately conservative — CEO Vinay Gupta repeatedly reframed "phenomenal" growth into modest 25–30% AUM CAGR guidance, prioritizing zero-NPA over headline growth ("our mission number one is not growth… it is zero NPA" — Anubhav Gupta). Candid on the equity-driven one-off inflating the 27% QoQ PBT, and on MoU numbers being a "dummy limit." Under-commit / over-deliver posture explicitly stated. Credible, granular answers on factoring mechanics and TAM.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The 27% QoQ PBT jump is not the run-rate** — ~Rs 337 cr of warrant equity landed end-Mar/early-Apr (absent in Q4), so normalized QoQ growth is ~14–15%; steady-state target is ~8–10% PAT QoQ.
- **Guidance was quietly raised** — FY30 AUM Rs 7,500 cr → Rs 10,000 cr and FY30 PAT Rs 375 cr looks beatable (Rs 225 cr already guided for FY27 alone), yet mgmt keeps the CAGR framing conservative.
- **Book value will lag earnings** by design — no dilution means fast EPS/PAT compounding won't show up proportionally in net worth (an analyst's point mgmt agreed with).
- **Factoring is strategically over-indexed vs its 5% AUM weight** — dedicated senior hires, RBI licence, "among ~1% of FIs" positioning suggest it's the next growth engine even though it's small today.

qoq change log (fill each quarter):

FY27 guide Rs 300 cr PBT / Rs 225 cr PAT / ~Rs 5,500 cr exit AUM, no equity raise. FY30 AUM guide raised to Rs 10,000 cr. Insurance-broker subsidiary incorporated (IRDAI pending). Factoring Rs 225 cr (~5% AUM).
- _Q2 FY27 → check: PAT ~8–10% QoQ delivery, AUM toward ~Rs 5,000 cr, NPA still nil, leverage creep toward 2.5x, IRDAI licence progress, any AIF/ARC/GIFT-City movement._

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Positions itself as a pure-play B2B supply chain finance NBFC — 'Empowering Businesses, Strengthening Supply Chains' — with supply chain financing explicitly stated as the continuing core business focus.
- Leverages parentage in the APL Apollo Group, whose flagship APL Apollo Tubes is described as India's largest structured steel manufacturer, giving anchor-corporate access to dealer and vendor ecosystems.
- Claims scarcity value as one of fewer than 1% of NBFCs offering Factoring and TReDS solutions, a regulatory/licensing moat in the supply chain financing space.
- Carries an ICRA rating of AA (CE) / A1+, supporting institutional funding access alongside a named panel of corporate and banking partners.
- States a 'deepening and widening' strategy: strengthening existing customer relationships, acquiring new customers, expanding products, forging partnerships and exploring adjacent financial services.

- **Factoring is strategically over-indexed vs its 5% AUM weight** — dedicated senior hires, RBI licence, "among ~1% of FIs" positioning suggest it's the next growth engine even though it's small today.
